# Grounding LLMs for Database Exploration: Intent Scoping and Paraphrasing for Robust NL2SQL

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#intent-scoping-paraphrasing)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://www.vldb.org/2025/Workshops/VLDB-Workshops-2025/AIDB/AIDB25_5.pdf) · AIDB 2025 workshop paper, 13 PDF pages

**Reading coverage:** Sections 1-8 and Appendix 9.1-9.6, Algorithms 1-3, Tables 1-8, Figures 1-9/captions and all prompt examples.

## Research question

Identify fully supported, partially supported and out-of-scope requests while diversifying NL2SQL training language without losing entities.

## Method

Combines schema-conditioned entity extraction, learned column-matching types, optional entity search and entity-preserving paraphrase generation. Scope labels rely on identified-column presence; paraphrasing is offline augmentation.

## Evaluation

Component studies use 70 entity-annotated Spider questions, 350 labeled columns and constructed scope cases. Downstream SFT/RAG comparisons cover Spider, BIRD and a proprietary five-table BI dataset.

## What the results support

Easy schema-based scope detection beats the direct-LLM baseline; adding search lowers BIRD accuracy. Paraphrase augmentation slightly improves BIRD/BI execution but decreases both reported Spider settings.

## Limits and qualifications

Schema removal creates partial-scope examples; it does not test complete user-guided recovery. Entity/cosine checks do not guarantee preserved intent. Components do not jointly demonstrate complex end-to-end SQL generation, and the BI data are proprietary.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Explicit partial answerability is valuable, but component accuracy and successful interactive resolution must remain distinct.

## Checks against the paper

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.

| Search improves scope detection. | BIRD Easy SD is 66.00% versus 56.00% with search. | Section 6.3/Table 3 | Do not imply extra retrieval consistently helps. |
| The framework enables reliable interactive exploration. | Section 8 leaves integration into a full system handling joins/nesting as future work. | Sections 5.4, 6.3 and 8 | Component-level evidence; no demonstrated end-to-end user study. |
